citations.assessment: The Yerushalmi identifies R. Kohen as Ḥiyya bar Abba’s brother. Their exchange concerns travel and prayer.

evidence.witness: The Jerusalem Talmud, edition by Heinrich W. Guggenheimer. Berlin, De Gruyter, 1999-2015

citations.assessment: Esther Rabbah explicitly uses the same brother designation in its opening material.
The reciprocal has a nearly identical travel and prayer story under Natan Kohen. Its local comparison supports recording the proposed identity without deciding it.
Bava Kamma gives all three in the same case, and the reciprocal under Avimi supplies the folio. This does not equate its Rav Kohen with the brother in the other passages.
